overview: Energy and utilities balance supply and demand second by second on physical networks that fail in the field. Weather, asset age and customer behaviour drive the data, outages carry safety and regulatory consequences, and control actions stay with licensed operators and protection systems.

concepts.name: Supply and demand must balance continuously
concepts.explanation: Electricity cannot be stored cheaply at scale, so generation, storage and demand response must match load in near real time. Forecast errors are paid for in reserves, imbalance charges or curtailment.
concepts.whyItMatters: A forecast is judged by what its error costs the operator, not only by its average error.

concepts.name: Renewable output depends on weather
concepts.explanation: Solar and wind generation follow irradiance, cloud cover and wind speed, with ramps that are hard to predict. Forecast quality varies by site, season and horizon.
concepts.whyItMatters: Probabilistic forecasts let operators size reserves, whereas point forecasts hide the risk.

concepts.name: Assets age and fail in the field
concepts.explanation: Transformers, cables, poles, pipes and pumps degrade with load, weather and time, and inspection data is sparse. Failures cause outages, safety incidents and environmental harm.
concepts.whyItMatters: Asset health models must support the decision to inspect, repair or replace, within a safety-first culture.

concepts.name: Outage management is a fault location problem
concepts.explanation: When a fault trips protection, operators locate it from smart meter, SCADA and customer calls, then restore supply in stages. Faster location shortens outage minutes.
concepts.whyItMatters: Customer minutes lost are the regulated measure, so restoration order matters as much as detection.

concepts.name: Smart meters produce large volumes of interval data
concepts.explanation: Meters report consumption at short intervals, which supports billing, loss detection and demand analytics but raises privacy concerns because the pattern reveals household behaviour.
concepts.whyItMatters: Analytics should use aggregation and access controls and avoid inferring sensitive household behaviour.

concepts.name: Losses and theft hide in the balance
concepts.explanation: Technical losses come from physics and non-technical losses from theft, metering and billing faults. Comparing energy in with energy billed by feeder points to where losses occur.
concepts.whyItMatters: Accusing customers on weak evidence harms trust, so cases need field verification.

concepts.name: Operators and protection systems hold control
concepts.explanation: Grid, gas and water operations are safety-critical and regulated. AI recommends and forecasts, while switching, dispatch and protection stay with licensed operators and certified systems.
concepts.whyItMatters: A recommendation that cannot be explained or overridden will not be used in a control room.

concepts.name: Field crews need practical work orders
concepts.explanation: Crew scheduling depends on location, skills, parts, access and permits. Plans that ignore these constraints fail on the day.
concepts.whyItMatters: A model that ranks jobs without capacity and travel produces schedules nobody can run.
